design.mechanism: An interlocutor treats rising vapour in both seasons as grounds to expect similar thunder. The answer distinguishes two intermediate production requirements that insufficient winter heat cannot meet: raising the required strong/stiff vapour and lifting it high enough for violent descent. A later attributed regional account instead makes excessive eastern summer heat disperse vapour and prevent its thickening into clouds. Eastern winter heat is compared explicitly with our summer, permitting the stated thunder account under a different place/season pairing. The two causal obstructions have different intermediate objects; neither is merely a reversal of one heat label.
design.contrast: R1: the presence of any rising vapour suffices for thunder. R2: heat has one unqualified monotonically increasing effect. R3: winter means the same thermal condition at every place, or thunder is absolutely absent in every winter. R4: both deficient and excessive heat prevent the same single stage. R5: eastern winter is compared with eastern summer or with our winter instead of our summer. R6: the attributed geographical report is treated as independent observation or a measured numeric optimum.
design.prediction: A faithful content account must preserve vapour rising even when the thunder requirements fail, distinguish inability to raise/elevate the appropriate vapour from excessive heat preventing cloud formation, and attach the gentle-winter comparison to eastern lands versus summer here. Merely listing heat, clouds, winter and summer loses the explanation. Reassigning the place of a season or swapping the blocked intermediate changes the stated reason and predicted seasonal pattern. No numerical thresholds, measured causal law or blanket absence of all winter thunder follows.
whole_source_duties: Exact complete local unit94.16–95.2 includes the opening question, both winter limitations, residual rain/snow/wind/non-lightning fires, autumn/spring rarity, attributed eastern seasonal contrast, and western comparison.
The initial winter question says not as in summer; do not strengthen it to no thunder in any winter. Autumn and spring explicitly retain a very-rare exception.
Winter heat cannot raise strong/stiff vapour as thunder requires AND cannot raise it sufficiently high for violent descent. No numerical amount, density, height or speed is given.

Eastern summer heat disperses vapour and prevents its becoming thick/clouds; this differs from inadequate lifting. Some say introduces the geographical report. No exact country or empirically demonstrated universal law is supplied.

Eastern winter heat is gentle like our summer; western lands are like here because summer is not excessively hot. The comparison objects, place and time scopes are written duties. Gentle and like express a qualitative local comparison, not equal measured temperatures or an optimal numerical band.
Earlier91.14–31 supplies warm/light vapour, cold-cloud repulsion, ignition/flame and tearing. The local seasonal argument assumes this historical process, not a modern replacement.
